found_values.value: 200 ms. No source names a deadline for the case itself: a frozen coprocessor beside a panel that keeps beating (docs/Safety.md:48-54 lists it as covered by no hardware). The tree bounds every stop path by the coprocessor's 200 ms link failsafe. LINK_DEV_SILENCE_MS is 200 (shared/link/include/link_dev.h:26-31: 'the processor holding the outputs is the more suspicious of the two'). The monostable page gives the deadline as 200 ms, 'the coprocessor's link failsafe; the backstop is not slower than the link' (hardware/docs/Monostable.md:28 and :115-116 at 23c82ca; IOBoard.md:186). The watchdog is the only stop path in this case, so this is the deadline applied to it. It is a deadline read from the tree, not an owner figure
found_values.source: shared/link/include/link_dev.h:26-31, docs/Safety.md:48-54 and hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:186 at commit c25aa86; hardware/docs/Monostable.md:28, :115-116 at commit 23c82ca

found_values.value: 900 ms with a host that stops reading, and no upper bound with a host that keeps accepting data more slowly than it is written. One main-loop pass can hold one flash window and then prints. The window is either a 4 kB sector erase (packaged W25Q16JV maximum 400 ms) or a page program (3 ms), never both in one pass (firmware/iomcu/src/main.c:1049-1087; out_store.c:337, :352, :376). A printf follows a window in the same pass (main.c:1057-1087), and can_report prints every 3 s (main.c:1089, :597-636). pico-sdk 2.3.0 and 2.3.1 stdio_usb_out_chars (stdio_usb.c:101-131, identical in both) waits while the host takes nothing, until PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US has passed since the last write the host accepted. That timeout defaults to 500,000 us (stdio_usb.h:31-33), and nothing under firmware/ overrides it. So: 400 ms + 500 ms = 900 ms. Each accepted write restarts the 500 ms, so a slow host sets no bound. Before CAN starts, the boot pass erases up to OUT_STORE_SECTORS = 2 sectors (out_store.h:122; main.c:937-942): 800 ms plus prints, if the watchdog is already running then. The 400 ms and 3 ms are packaged-part figures; the die's are not known

found_values.value: 1000 ppm total: tolerance, stability over temperature and ageing together. Section 8.1.2.3 says 'Appropriate margin is built into the design to tolerate up to 1000ppm variation in the XOSC frequency'. The PLL section says the PLLs 'can drive clocks at their maximum frequency as long as the reference clock is accurate to 1000ppm'. The other limits are all looser. USB full speed requires 12.000 Mb/s +/-0.25 %, 2,500 ppm (USB 2.0 section 7.1.11, TFDRATE 11.97 to 12.03 Mb/s in Table 7-8). The bidirectional DShot decoder is tested at +/-5 %, and the ESC takes +/-2 % of that (V3, owner), which leaves +/-3 %, 30,000 ppm. The CAN bit rate depends on this crystal only if R2 clocks its controller from the RP2354B
found_values.source: RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29 (build-version d126e9e-clean), sections 8.1.2.3 and 8.1 (PLL paragraph), https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rp2350/rp2350-datasheet.pdf served from https://pip-assets.raspberrypi.com/categories/1214-rp2350/documents/RP-008373-DS-2-rp2350-datasheet.pdf (SHA-256 2877d0f2...4be8); USB 2.0 specification usb_20.pdf section 7.1.11, in https://www.usb.org/sites/default/files/usb_20_20250603.zip (read 2026-09-28T12:53:21Z); test/host/test_dshot_telem.c:197-217; V3

found_values.value: load capacitance 10 pF; ESR at most 50 Ohm; drive-level rating at least 200 uW. Table 597 gives the crystal the XOSC circuit is tuned for (ABM8-272-T3) as CL 10 pF, ESR (R1) 50 Ohm max, and drive level 10 uW typical, 200 uW max. The hardware design guide, section 4, says: 'We've opted for a device with a maximum of 50 Ohm, as we've found that this, along with a 1 kOhm series resistor (R2), is a good value to prevent the crystal being over-driven and being damaged when using an IOVDD level of 3.3 V'. It also says the 10 pF load is two 15 pF capacitors plus about 3 pF of stray capacitance. The drive level the circuit actually applies is not stated in either document. The 200 uW is the rated maximum of the crystal the circuit is tuned for, and is applied as the lowest rating a crystal may have
found_values.source: RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29, section 8.2.1.1, Table 597; Hardware design with RP2350, section 4 and 4.1, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rp2350/hardware-design-with-rp2350.pdf served from https://pip-assets.raspberrypi.com/categories/1214-rp2350/documents/RP-008280-DS-2-hardware-design-with-rp2350.pdf (PDF created 2026-08-20, read 2026-09-28T12:51:45Z)

found_values.value: The USB 2.0 limits: at most 75 pF of lumped capacitance to ground per line on D+ and on D-, shared by the transceiver pin, the connector and the protection. The whole upstream-facing full-speed port with a detachable cable may have at most 100 pF (CINUB): the 75 pF lumped plus 25 pF on each conductor between receptacle and transceiver. D+ and D- must differ by less than 10 %. The RP2350 datasheet gives no capacitance for USB_DP and USB_DM (Table 1437). The share left for the protection is therefore 75 pF less the pin and connector capacitance, which is not known
found_values.source: USB 2.0 specification usb_20.pdf, section 7.1.6.1 and Table 7-7 (CINUB 100 pF, CEDGE 75 pF), in https://www.usb.org/sites/default/files/usb_20_20250603.zip; RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29, Table 1437

found_values.value: not found at the primary source. The RP2350 datasheet (build 2025-07-29) gives no voltage rating for USB_DP and USB_DM. They are typed 'USB IO' on USB_OTP_VDD (Tables 1426, 1431). Table 1433 rates only Standard pins (VPIN, IOVDD + 0.5 V) and FT pins, and Table 1437 gives no maximum input voltage. The only ESD figures are component-level: 2 kV HBM on all pins and 500 V CDM (Table 1434). USB 2.0 section 7.1.1, as changed by the '5V Short Circuit Withstand' ECN, makes a transceiver's withstand of a short to VBUS (5.25 V) a recommendation only. So neither a clamping limit nor a highest steady voltage for these pins is stated. The value is not applied as a requirement

report.value: Errata affecting A4 (Appendix E; Appendix C: A4 is CHIP_ID.REVISION 0x8 with no hardware changes over A3): E1 interpolator OVERF bits broken (SIO interpolator). E2 SIO SPINLOCK writes mirrored at +0x80 (SIO). E4 System Bus Access stalls while core 1 is in clock-gated sleep (RISC-V debug SBA; do not use SBA, or do not set DEEPSLEEP on core 1). E5 DMA CHAIN_TO with ABORT of active channels (DMA; clear EN on the aborted channel and on every channel it chains to, as firmware/iomcu/src/out_ppm.c:68-80 does). E6 PMPCFGx RWX transposed and E7 U-mode does not ignore mstatus.mie (Hazard3 RISC-V only). E8 CHAIN_TO may not fire for zero-length transfers (DMA; no zero-length transfers in chains). E11 XIP cache clean by set/way retags dirty lines (XIP; use xip_cache_clean_all()). E12 USB status signals under-synchronised (USB; run clk_sys at least 10 % faster than clk_usb while the peripheral is in use, 52.8 MHz for a 48 MHz clk_usb; mitigated for the bootrom only on A3). E17 guarded single-row ECC OTP read faults. E26 RCP random delays side channel. E27 BUS_PRIORITY miswired on the APB and FASTPERI arbiters (DMA against core priority at peripherals). E28 OTP keys for pages 62/63 apply to all lock words. E5, E8, E12, E27, E1, E2 and E11 constrain a peripheral. None constrains a pin, a pull resistor or an input front end. RP2350-E9 (Bank 0 leakage with pad input enabled) affects A2 only and is fixed in A3; E3 is A2 QFN-60 only; E16 is A2 only
report.source: RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29, Appendix C and Appendix E, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rp2350/rp2350-datasheet.pdf (SHA-256 2877d0f270fb6d6a57943bee58aaad536aa027bea1e5b1c4ce2541a3230d4be8), read 2026-09-28T12:51:17Z

report.value: Confirmed in build 2025-07-29, where the tables are numbered 3 higher than in build 2024-08-08. GPIO0-39 on QFN-80 are Digital IO (FT) (Table 1427). VPIN_FT is -0.5 V to 5.5 V at IOVDD 3.3 V ('IOVDD must be present'), 4.2 V at 2.5 V, and 3.63 V at 1.8 V and at IOVDD 0 V (Table 1433). GPIO40-47 are Digital IO / Analogue, VPIN (Standard) -0.5 V to IOVDD + 0.5 V (Table 1433), and the ADC input range is 0 to ADC_AVDD (Table 1438). RUN (35), SWCLK (33) and SWDIO (34) are FT (Table 1430). The QSPI pins, QSPI_SS (75) among them, are standard IO on QSPI_IOVDD, not FT (Table 1428). USB_DP and USB_DM are USB IO with no voltage rating in Table 1433. Current into an FT pin below 3.63 V with IOVDD at 0 V: 'very little current', no figure (Table 1426). ESD: HBM 2 kV on all pins, 4 kV on FT pins; CDM 500 V (Table 1434). IOVDD and QSPI_IOVDD absolute maximum 3.63 V. These equal the figures IOBoard.md:54 and :105 cite, so P5 has no differing figure to re-check pull request #167 against: its statement on an absent IOVDD holds for GPIO40-47 and not for GPIO0-39. Build 2024-08-08 itself was not read

Table 1436 (Standard and FT pins): IIN max 1 uA, with no IOVDD condition. RPU 32-86 kOhm at IOVDD 3.3 V (32-106 at 1.8 V, 42-123 at 2.5 V). RPD 36-113 kOhm at 3.3 V. At 3.3 V: VIH min 2 V (FT max 5.5 V), VIL max 0.8 V, hysteresis min 0.2 V, VOH min 2.62 V, VOL max 0.5 V. Total IOVDD source current 100 mA, QSPI_IOVDD 20 mA. Reset states: GPIO0-47 pull-down (Table 1427); SWDIO pin 34, SWCLK pin 33 and RUN pin 35 pull-up (Table 1430); QSPI_SS pin 75, SD2 and SD3 pull-up, SCLK, SD0 and SD1 pull-down (Table 1428). USB IO (Table 1437): IIN 1 uA, RPD 14.25-15.75 kOhm, RPU2 0.873-1.548 kOhm, RPU1&2 1.398-3.063 kOhm. These equal IOBoard.md:105 and :122

Part number W25Q16JVWI, read from Raspberry Pi's own copy (section 14.3). The six QSPI pads reach both the flash die and the package pins. The flash's PADRESETB is not connected, so the flash die has no hardware reset. Maximum QSPI clock 133 MHz. Supply: QSPI_IOVDD 2.7 to 3.6 V (section 14.3), and QSPI_IOVDD on the RP2354 2.97 to 3.63 V, 3.3 V typical (Table 1441); together 2.97 to 3.60 V, which holds 3.3 V +/-3 %. Erase, program and endurance of the W25Q16JVWI die: not known; the public ordering list names no W-suffix part and says 'Contact Winbond for KGD'. Packaged-part figures, marked as such (W25Q16JV-DTR revision I, published 2026-05-28): 4 kB sector erase 45 ms typ and 400 ms max, 256-byte page program 0.4 ms typ and 3 ms max, 32 kB block erase 1,600 ms max, 64 kB block erase 2,000 ms max, at least 100,000 program-erase cycles

report.value: Yes: 1 kOhm in series between the BOOT contact and QSPI_SS (QFN-80 pin 75). The hardware design guide (section 3.1) wires the USB_BOOT button to QSPI_SS through R6, 1 kOhm: 'It is important to include resistor R6, as this allows the QSPI_SS pin to safely over-drive the applied pull-down when the RP2350 starts booting'. For the RP2354 it keeps the USB_BOOT switch on QSPI_SS with the external flash removed. The datasheet (section 14.3) says CSn driven low at reset 'harmlessly selects the internal flash die but does not issue commands to it'. On the IO board, the BOOT button and the bench relay contact across it both reach QSPI_SS through that one resistor. The guide's optional 10 kOhm pull-up on QSPI_SS (R1, not fitted) was found unnecessary for its W25Q128JV. For the in-package W25Q16JVWI this is not stated
report.source: Hardware design with RP2350, section 3.1, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rp2350/hardware-design-with-rp2350.pdf, read 2026-09-28T12:51:45Z; RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29, section 14.3 and Table 1428

report.value: By source reading, target/rp2350.cfg reaches the RP2354B and programs its in-package flash; this is not tested on an RP2354B. The config attaches to the RP2350 die over SWD (CPUTAPID 0x00040927, ADIv6 DAP, Cortex-M33 cores at AP 0x2000 and 0x4000). It defines 'flash bank $_CHIPNAME.flash rp2xxx 0x10000000 $_FLASHSIZE', with the size detected when FLASHSIZE is 0. The rp2xxx driver erases and programs through the bootrom's connect_internal_flash, flash_range_erase and flash_range_program on QSPI chip select 0. Section 14.3 of the datasheet connects that chip select to the in-package W25Q16JVWI. Size detection reads the JEDEC ID and falls back to SFDP. The ID table carries 'win w25q16jv' 0x1540ef and 0x1570ef at 2 MB (spi.c:132-133). Whether the W25Q16JVWI die returns EF 40 15 is not stated in a public document; SFDP, or FLASHSIZE 0x200000, covers either case. The bench's OpenOCD 0.12.0+dev snapshot of 2026-02-16 postdates the driver's last change (2025-06-29) and rp2350.cfg's change of 2026-02-15. Erratum E4 matters only for RISC-V SBA, which rp2350.cfg does not select by default
report.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openocd-org/openocd/master/tcl/target/rp2350.cfg and src/flash/nor/rp2xxx.c (read 2026-09-28T12:56:43Z), src/flash/nor/spi.c (12:57:03Z); GitHub commits API for those paths (12:56:52Z, 12:57:13Z); RP2350 datasheet section 14.3; testbench/README.md:456-465

report.value: The RP2350 watchdog counts down from LOAD, maximum 0xffffff, 'approximately 16 seconds' (section 12.9), ticked from the ticks block. pico-sdk's _watchdog_enable clamps the load to that maximum and can pause on debug (section 12.9.6.1). The coprocessor image sets none (V4). Longest legitimate stall found (V2): 900 ms for one pass, a 400 ms packaged-part sector erase plus a USB printf blocked up to 500,000 us. There is no bound while a host accepts data more slowly than it is written. Up to 800 ms of boot-time erases follow if the watchdog is enabled before them. Stop deadline found (V1): 200 ms. No timeout satisfies both, because 900 ms > 200 ms; the 400 ms erase alone exceeds 200 ms. Reported to the owner: the conflict holds while the output binding stays in the in-package flash (Q8) and the console print can block for PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US
report.source: RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29, section 12.9, read 2026-09-28T12:51:17Z; V1, V2, V4 as found (see found_values)

report.value: Lines of pico-sdk 2.3.0 boards/olimex_rp2350_xl.h that the IO board's header keeps: :17 PICO_PLATFORM rp2350, :25 PICO_RP2350A 0 (48 GPIO), :73 PICO_BOOT_STAGE2_CHOOSE_W25Q080 1, :75-77 PICO_FLASH_SPI_CLKDIV 2, :79-82 PICO_FLASH_SIZE_BYTES 2 MB, and no PSRAM chip select. Lines it changes: :14-15 include guard and :22 OLIMEX_RP2350_XL board-detection define, renamed for the IO board; :28-36 PICO_DEFAULT_UART 0 on GPIO0/1, which the image does not use (stdio on USB only, CMakeLists.txt:98-99) and which moves to the IO board's pin map; :39-41 PICO_DEFAULT_LED_PIN 25; :44-52 PICO_DEFAULT_I2C 1 on GPIO2/3; :55-69 PICO_DEFAULT_SPI 0 on GPIO4-7, all set from the IO board's pin map or removed; :84-87 PICO_RP2350_A2_SUPPORTED 1, which the A4 stepping (owner) lets go to 0

+/-30 ppm at 25 C, +/-30 ppm stability over -40 to +85 C, +/-5 ppm first-year ageing: +/-65 ppm total. This is within the 1000 ppm XOSC margin (V5), the 2,500 ppm of USB full speed, and the +/-3 % the DShot decoder leaves beside a +/-2 % ESC (V3). The CAN bit rate depends on it only if R2 clocks its controller from the RP2354B
